message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of move‑in condition (photos, inventory). | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep premises in good repair and free of health hazards. | • Report problems promptly; document all communications. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withhold** | • If landlord fails to fix major repairs within 30 days after notice, tenant may pay the amount needed to fix it and deduct from rent, or withhold rent until repaired. | • Keep receipts and proof of payment. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) except emergencies. | • Document any unauthorized entries. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For nonpayment: 3‑day written notice before eviction.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice if lease is month‑to‑month. | • Use certified mail or personal delivery with receipt. | | **Eviction Process** | • Must follow court procedure; unlawful detainer suit requires proper notice and filing. | • Tenants can contest eviction in court; they have a right to a hearing. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, source of income, etc. | • File complaint with Texas Commission on Human Rights or U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Lease Terms** | • Landlord cannot impose unreasonable restrictions (e.g., banning pets unless justified). | • Lease must be in writing for month‑to‑month agreements. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent‑control laws. | • Rent increases must comply with lease terms or give required notice. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, heat, and electricity unless otherwise agreed. | • Verify utility responsibilities in lease. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord not required to insure tenant’s property. | • Tenants should consider renter’s insurance. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, emails, and receipts help prove your case. 2. **Use Certified Mail** – For notices to landlord or to serve legal documents. 3. **Know the Timeline** – Texas law sets strict deadlines for notices and actions. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or discrimination, contact local legal aid organizations or the Texas Attorney General’s Office. 5. **File Complaints** – For housing code violations, file with the Texas Commission on Fire Safety or local building department. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 24 (Landlord‑Tenant Law) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – Discrimination complaints - **Texas Attorney General** – Consumer protection and housing resources - **Local Legal Aid** – e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, Houston Legal Aid Society --- If you need a specific lease template or a legal document tailored to your situation, let me know and I can generate a contract using the provided tool.
